text:
Hi, thanks for connecting. We're looking to place an order for 200 units of your 12V 100Ah LiFePO4 battery packs. Delivery within 30 days of order confirmation is essential for us, so please let me know upfront if that timeline works on your end.

On pricing, we're hoping to land around $44 per unit at this volume — can you share your best quote for 200 units? Also curious about your standard lead times and whether the 30-day window is feasible given current stock/production.

Looking forward to your numbers.

Thanks for the details. I want to be transparent that I can’t commit to 200 units within 30 days. I can offer 150 units at $44 each, shipped on day 40, with free freight and net-30 terms.

I may be able to source the remaining 50 units separately, but their availability, pricing, and timing would require written approval before I could confirm them. If you have flexibility on the 30-day requirement, I’d be glad to structure the 150-unit shipment as the firm first tranche and pursue approval for the balance.

Would a day-40 shipment for 150 units, with the remaining 50 handled as a separately approved tranche, be workable?

Hi, thanks for the honesty on where things stand. Unfortunately 200 units within 30 days is a firm requirement on our end — we can't split the order into separate tranches with uncertain timing and approval for the second batch, since that leaves us exposed on both quantity and schedule.

I understand production/stock may be tight, but before we look elsewhere, I want to give you a chance to work the timeline. Is there any way to expedite so the full 200 units ship within 30 days, even if it means a modest premium over $44 to prioritize our order? We have some room on price if it means hitting the date and the full quantity — but both the 200-unit volume and the 30-day window are non-negotiable for us.

Can you check with your production/logistics team on what it would take to compress the timeline for the full order, and what that would cost?

I appreciate the opportunity, but I don’t want to overpromise. I’m not authorized to commit to either 200 units or shipment within 30 days, and the required written director approval is not available during your purchasing window. Our firm capability remains 150 units shipping no earlier than day 40.

Since both the full quantity and 30-day timeline are non-negotiable, we can’t responsibly meet this order’s requirements. I understand you’ll need to pursue another supplier, and I’d welcome the chance to support a future order with more lead time.
